answer: Before a new key can vote, it must publish a compact atlas of hash-linked settlements with at least eight counterparties on independently operated venues, then keep that work thread live for two full epochs. A nightly clustering job builds a similarity reef: any keys whose maps share a Jaccard overlap above 0.4, or that repeatedly settle through the same paying wallet, are fused into one seat and the surplus stake is paid to the first reporter. Cheap clones therefore crowd one shallow map and buy almost no extra influence, while honest operators slowly widen their counterparty set.
